references.text: Jesus gives a similar command to the disciples to cast the net on the other side of the boat after the resurrection, resulting in a miraculous catch, parallel to the event in Luke 5.
The immediate context: Simon obeys Jesus' words even though they had fished all night without catching anything, and the result is an overwhelming catch of fish.
Jesus shows his power over nature by calming the storm on the sea, just as here he demonstrates his power over nature by providing a miraculous fishing catch.
God's word does not return empty but accomplishes what he desires – Jesus' words to Simon about casting the nets lead to a concrete, abundant result, an expression of the effectiveness of God's word.
The sea belongs to the Lord, vast and wide, filled with fish – Jesus' command to fish in deep water shows his dominion over the sea and its creatures.
Ezekiel's vision of water flowing from the temple bringing life and an abundance of fish, a picture of God's blessing and plenty reflected in the miraculous catch that Jesus provides.

The result of Jesus' command in verse 4: Simon and his companions leave everything and follow Jesus, and they will henceforth catch people – the deeper meaning behind the command to go out into the deep.
Matthew's parallel account of the calling of Simon and Andrew by the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus calls them to become fishers of men.
